ticket: W1-01 — Multi-language Tree-sitter parsing module (GAPFILL: GAP-5/6/7/8)
goal: Close the four non-OK findings from the W1-01 audit: make the JS/TS tree-sitter capture set see `export … from "…"` re-exports, generator functions, TypeScript `import x = require("y")`, and class expressions — and commit fixtures + regenerated goldens so the snapshot suite can actually catch a regression of any of them. This is an additive extraction delta inside the existing query/adapter design, not a redesign of the parsing module.

acceptanceCriteria.text: (GAP-5) In a .js, .jsx, .ts and .tsx file, each of `export * from "./a";`, `export { b } from "./b";` and `export * as ns from "./c";` produces exactly one ParsedImport with `module` equal to the raw, unresolved source string ("./a" / "./b" / "./c") and `start_line` at the statement. parse_full on a barrel file containing all three returns three imports, where it previously returned [].

(GAP-5) Re-export `symbols` follow exactly these rules: `export * from "m"` -> []; `export { a, b as c } from "m"` -> ["a", "b"] (original pre-alias names, matching _import_symbols); `export * as ns from "m"` -> ["ns"]; `export type { T } from "m"` -> ["T"]. `is_relative` is True for ./ or ../ module strings and False otherwise.

(GAP-6) `function* g(){}`, `export function* g(){}` and `async function* g(){}` each produce one ParsedFunction with name/qualified_name `g`, in both the javascript and typescript/tsx grammars. A file containing only `function* genFn(){ yield 1; }` returns one function, where it previously returned [] while still listing the file in parsed_files.
(GAP-6) `const g = function* () {};` produces one ParsedFunction named `g`, spanning the generator-expression node, consistent with how `const g = function(){}` is handled today.

(GAP-6) A generator function is a scope: a function declared inside `function* outer()` has qualified_name == "outer.inner", and a call site inside outer has caller_qualified_name == "outer". A generator method inside a class still yields enclosing_class == "<Class>" and qualified_name == "<Class>.<method>".

(GAP-7) In a .ts/.tsx file, `import fs = require("fs");` produces one ParsedImport with module == "fs", symbols == ["fs"], is_relative == False; and `import util = require("./util");` produces module == "./util", symbols == ["util"], is_relative == True. A file mixing an import-equals with an ordinary `import { A } from "./a";` returns both, in start_line order.

(GAP-7) `const C = class { m() {} };` produces one ParsedClass named `C` and its method as ParsedFunction(name="m", qualified_name="C.m", enclosing_class="C") — not, as today, a top-level qualified_name == "m" with the binding lost and no class at all.

(GAP-7) `const D = class extends Legacy {};` produces one ParsedClass named `D` with base_names == ["Legacy"] and exactly one ParsedInheritance(subclass_qualified_name="D", base_name="Legacy"), in both the JS and TS heritage shapes.

(GAP-8) The committed fixture dirs tests/fixtures/parsing/javascript/ and tests/fixtures/parsing/typescript/ each contain source exercising every construct in AC-1..AC-8 that applies to them, including at least one .tsx file exercising a re-export, a generator and a class expression under the tsx grammar. test_parse_full_matches_golden_snapshot passes for all four languages against regenerated goldens.

(GAP-8) The regenerated goldens demonstrably contain the new records: the JS and TS expected_parse.json diffs add ParsedImport rows for each new re-export/import-equals, a ParsedFunction row for each new generator, and a ParsedClass (plus ParsedInheritance where applicable) row for each new class expression. Reverting any one of the five new query patterns makes test_parse_full_matches_golden_snapshot fail — i.e. the snapshot suite can now catch GAP-5/6/7 regressions, which is exactly what it could not do before.

(GAP-8) tests/fixtures/parsing/mixed/expected_parse.json exists and is asserted by a snapshot test, and the expected_parse.json exclusion lives in _load_fixture_repo() in both test_parsing.py and test_parsing_tester.py. test_parse_full_over_mixed_language_repo's `assert skipped_paths == {"README.md"}` and test_parse_full_and_parse_diff_agree_on_mixed_language_fileset are unchanged and still pass.

(GAP-5, GAP-6, GAP-7) Documentation matches behaviour: both .scm header comments, adapters/javascript.py's module docstring, adapters/typescript.py's docstring (which currently claims the two query files have identical patterns) and parsing/__init__.py's exclusions list all describe the newly captured constructs, and still name the deliberately excluded forms (anonymous default-export generator, unbound/anonymous class expression, TS namespace alias `import A = B.C;`, local `export { a };`).

(GAP-8) A test compiles queries/javascript.scm against the javascript grammar and queries/typescript.scm against both the typescript and tsx grammars, and fails loudly if any pattern references a node type the grammar does not define. Without this, a bad pattern degrades into SkippedFile(reason="parse_error") for every JS/TS file rather than an error.

edgeCases.text: (GAP-5) A local export with no `from` clause (`const a = 1; export { a };`) produces no ParsedImport. It is not a module dependency.

(GAP-5) A declaration export (`export function f(){}`, `export const x = 1;`, `export default class K {}`, `export class L {}`) produces no ParsedImport, and the declaration itself is still extracted exactly as it is today (no regression from the new export_statement pattern).
(GAP-5) A bare-package re-export (`export { x } from "lodash";`) sets is_relative == False; `export * from "../shared";` sets is_relative == True.

(GAP-5) A file that both imports from and re-exports the same module (`import { a } from "./m"; export { b } from "./m";`) produces two ParsedImport rows for "./m" — no deduplication — ordered by start_line per _parse()'s existing sort key.
(GAP-6) `export default function* () {}` (anonymous generator) produces no ParsedFunction, consistent with the existing anonymous default-export function rule.

(GAP-6) An anonymous generator passed inline (`run(function* () { yield 1; });`) produces no ParsedFunction, consistent with anonymous callbacks/IIFEs (GAP-9's documented exclusion), and the surrounding run(...) is still recorded as a ParsedCall.

(GAP-6) Generator methods (`class S { *rows(){} async *arows(){} }`) are captured exactly once each after the change — adding generator patterns must not double-emit anything method_definition already covered.
(GAP-7) A TS namespace alias with no require (`import A = B.C;`) produces no ParsedImport — it has no module string. This is why the pattern is (import_require_clause) rather than (import_statement).

(GAP-7) `import fs = require("fs");` in a .js file (not valid JS) parses error-tolerantly: no exception escapes extract(), the file still appears in parsed_files, and it does not become a SkippedFile. Whatever partial records tree-sitter yields are acceptable; the requirement is no crash and no blanket skip.

(GAP-7) Unbound/anonymous class expressions produce no ParsedClass: `foo(class { m(){} });`, `this.C = class {};`, `export default class {};`, `const [x] = [class {}];` (destructuring pattern, not a plain identifier declarator).
(GAP-7) `const C = class Inner { m(){} };` produces exactly one ParsedClass (named C per _class_expression_binding's precedence), never two, and m qualifies as C.m.
(GAP-7) A class expression nested inside a function (`function f(){ const C = class { m(){} }; }`) chains correctly: C.qualified_name == "f.C", m.qualified_name == "f.C.m", m.enclosing_class == "C".

(GAP-8) Golden regeneration cannot mask a regression: the committed goldens are the hand-verified diff, and UPDATE_PARSE_SNAPSHOTS is not set anywhere in .github/workflows/ci.yml or in services/workers/ config, so CI asserts rather than rewrites.

(all) Malformed source containing a targeted construct is best-effort and never fatal: `export * from` with no module string, `export { a, } from "./m";` (trailing comma), `function* (` truncated mid-declaration, `const C = class extends` truncated. extract() raises nothing, parser.py records no parse_error skip, and the file stays in parsed_files.

(all) Determinism is preserved for the new records: parse_full over the extended javascript/ and typescript/ fixture dirs is byte-identical under reversed input order, and to_canonical_json(parse_full(files)) == to_canonical_json(parse_diff(files, deleted_paths=[])) for those same dirs.

(all) No spurious extraction: a JS/TS file containing none of the new constructs produces the same records as before the change. Concretely, the existing fixture sources (javascript/index.js, javascript/shapes.js, javascript/widget.jsx, typescript/models.ts, typescript/widget.tsx) contribute no added or altered rows to the regenerated goldens — the golden diff consists only of records from the newly added fixture files plus the new parsed_files entries.

(GAP-8) Empty input still holds: parse_full([]) returns an all-empty ParseResult, and a fixture dir containing only non-source files yields only skipped_files. The _load_fixture_repo() change must not alter this.
